Indefatigable

/in-dih-FAT-ih-guh-buhl/ - the stress falls on FAT · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Indefatigable means never tiring; persisting without rest.

Reporters assigned to the indefatigable senator work in relays: four town halls, two factory tours, and a late-night diner stop, all inside a single Monday.

Worked Example

At mile eighty of the hundred-mile trail race, the pacers who had taken turns beside Ruiz were done — calves cramping, headlamps dimming, one asleep in a folding chair. Ruiz's stride at mile ninety matched her stride at mile ten, and at the finish she asked, quite seriously, where breakfast was. Her crew calls her indefatigable and schedules its own naps around the fact.

Indefatigable makes a stronger claim than hardworking or determined: not that the effort is great, but that the well it draws from never empties. Inside the word sits de- + fatigare, 'to tire out completely' — negated. This is the person the work cannot wear down, however long it runs.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

tireless: Tireless says in plain English what indefatigable says in Latin dress: the person does not grow weary, no matter how long the work runs. Being the everyday word, tireless fits small heroics — a tireless den mother — while indefatigable rolls a drum and suits effort on a grand, public scale.

unflagging: Unflagging attaches to the effort rather than the person: unflagging energy, unflagging enthusiasm, support that never loses force or pace. Indefatigable describes the human being who supplies all of that — the campaigner or night nurse whom the work itself cannot wear down.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

weary: worn down and ready to stop

flagging: losing steam mid-course

Where it sits · how long the stamina holds out — energetic → persistent → indefatigable

energetic vs. indefatigable: Energetic says the tank is full this morning and promises nothing about tonight; indefatigable promises the whole season — the tank never empties.

persistent vs. indefatigable: The persistent keep going through setbacks, tired or not; indefatigable goes further — the tiredness never comes at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-

Prefix — in-: not

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: completely

Root — fatig

Root — fatig: to tire (Latin fatigare)

Suffix — -able

Suffix — -able: able to be

Put it together

Put it together: In- (not) + de- (completely) + fatig (to tire, from Latin fatigare) + -able (able to be) = not able to be completely tired out. Four gears mesh into one long word, and the length earns its keep: defatigare meant to exhaust utterly, and indefatigable slams the in- across the whole idea. Whoever wears the word cannot be worn out.

Word Choice

admiring / formal

Indefatigable is the long word you earn by never stopping — campaigners, archivists, nurses on doubled shifts. Tireless says the same thing in plainer clothes; indefatigable adds a drumroll, so spend it on effort that genuinely never flags, not on one productive afternoon.
